turns.text: real quick how long does caffeine from a cold brew last. i quit energy drinks monday and now just have one cold brew before shift

Caffeine usually peaks 30-60 minutes after you drink it. The half-life is about 5-6 hours, so half is still in your system around the midpoint of a long night, and a meaningful amount lingers 8-10 hours. Individual metabolism varies a lot. How big is the cold brew, and when do you drink it relative to your start time?
16oz. my shift is 9pm to 730am ten hours. trevor picks me up before so i grab it around 8:15 while im waiting on him

A 16 oz cold brew typically has about 200-300 mg of caffeine depending on the shop, versus roughly 160 mg in a 16 oz energy drink can, so your one cold brew is likely equal to or more than the two cans. Sipping it at 8:15 puts the peak right around when you clock in at 9, and by about 2-3 a.m. you'd be at roughly half. If you hit a wall there, a small top-up around 1 a.m. (like 50-100 mg) would carry you to the end better than one big dose. Try to keep your last caffeine at least 6 hours before you plan to sleep. If you tell me the exact brand I can narrow the number.
ok so about 250 prob. cant do math this early lol. also does caffeine mess with how cold u get? i work the cold dock and the cold gets to me

Short version: caffeine can narrow blood vessels near the skin a bit, which may make your hands and feet feel colder, but it doesn't change how well your body holds core heat in a meaningful way. The bigger factors are layers, insulated gloves, moving regularly, and eating enough, since being under-fueled makes cold feel worse. If your fingers get especially cold, a warm drink or hand warmers in your pockets will help more than changing your caffeine. Keeping the cold brew at 250 mg and spacing it as above is a reasonable plan.
